guarantees.claim: unused_cfg_qe is assigned the XOR reduction of cfg_reg fields sha_en.qe, hmac_en.qe, endian_swap.qe, digest_swap.qe, key_swap.qe, digest_size.qe, and key_length.qe.
sha_en is assigned the value of cfg_reg.sha_en.q.
hmac_en is assigned the value of cfg_reg.hmac_en.q.
digest_size_supplied is assigned cfg_reg.digest_size.q cast to digest_mode_e.

assumptions.claim: cfg_reg.digest_size.q must encode a valid member of the digest_mode_e enum.
assumptions.cond: when digest_size_supplied is used by downstream logic
assumptions.risk: if violated, digest_size_supplied may carry an undefined or reserved enum value, causing downstream digest control to choose an unexpected digest length or error route, potentially weakening HMAC security or causing functional failure.

uncertain_points.claim: The assignment digest_size_supplied = digest_mode_e'(cfg_reg.digest_size.q) does not validate that the register value corresponds to a legal enum member. A software write with an invalid encoding will propagate a corrupted digest size.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes an unsupported value to cfg_reg.digest_size
uncertain_points.risk: downstream digest logic could behave in an unspecified way, possibly producing truncated digests or entering an undefined state, which may impact HMAC integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_cfg_qe is assigned but not used in this chunk (and presumably only serves as a lint waiver). If it is never consumed elsewhere, it may represent dead logic.
uncertain_points.risk: No direct functional risk, but may obscure missing functional uses of the qe signals or indicate unnecessary fan-out.
